assert.add.what: state what has to be true for a run to have passed, so a scripted run ends with a verdict rather than a table somebody has to read

params.name: kind
params.what: what is measured: `delivered` (or `deliveries`, or `unique_deliveries`) counts the nodes that heard anything, `sent` (or `transmissions`) counts transmissions; absent is refused, and a kind this build does not understand is accepted here and fails at the check rather than passing

params.name: node
params.what: restrict a transmission count to one node; has to be named, and absent counts every node

params.name: at_least
params.what: the floor the count has to reach; absent is zero, which any count clears

params.name: at_most
params.what: the ceiling, which a transmission count uses in place of at_least whenever it is above zero

params.name: max_pct
params.what: recorded on the assertion and carried in the fixture, and read by no kind this build checks

params.name: within_ms
params.what: recorded on the assertion and carried in the fixture, and read by no kind this build checks

assert.add.answers: `assertions` is how many the scenario now carries, not the one just added.

example.what: the flood has to reach at least two nodes

assert.check.what: measure every assertion against the run so far and report each one separately, which is what a scripted run exits on
assert.check.answers: `results` is one row per assertion, carrying `kind`, `node`, `pass`, `got` and `want`. A scenario carrying no assertions is refused rather than answered with a pass, and an assertion whose kind this build does not understand fails with `got` reading "not measured": a green run that checked nothing is the failure this guards against.

schedule.add.what: have a node originate traffic on its own at a stated moment of simulated time, so a run reproduces without anybody watching it for the moment to press send

params.name: node
params.what: the node that sends; absent is refused, and so is a name no node in this network carries

params.name: at_ms
params.what: the simulated instant of the first send; absent is zero, which is the start of the run

params.name: every_ms
params.what: repeat interval in simulated milliseconds; absent or zero sends once

params.name: command
params.what: what the node is told to do, in its own console's words; has to be named rather than passed bare, and absent leaves it empty

schedule.add.answers: `sends` is how many the schedule now holds, not the one just added.

example.what: one flood thirty seconds into the run

schedule.clear.what: empty the schedule, which is what editing it amounts to: nothing removes a single send, so a schedule is rebuilt rather than amended
